# Russian morphology provenance

This package contains the Russian dictionary runtime from Andrew Kovalenko's
[libmorph](https://github.com/big-keva/libmorph), revision
`90a5a1a95d0edf693855f6b66759c8b66821865f`, and the required conversion tables
from [moonycode](https://github.com/big-keva/moonycode), revision
`639553712ab068315ba9726d56989956962048b3`.
Both use the MIT license; the complete licenses and source notices are preserved.

The six `.bin` files are lossless lexical tables generated from that libmorph
revision's complete `lang-rus/dict/*.dic`, flexion and interchange tables. They
are dictionary data, not neural model weights. `dictionary-manifest.json` records
their exact lengths, SHA-256 hashes and combined resource identity. Their total
is 3,841,191 bytes. `DictionaryData.S` embeds them in a read-only binary section,
avoiding a mutable loader, runtime downloads and large generated C++ files.

The package vendors the runtime subset only. Generator-only dependency
[mtc](https://github.com/big-keva/mtc), revision
`cb2c4deb1f6d02e24b54eea827f5688c64b6879f`, is not distributed or linked in the app.
Regeneration uses its committed source and a documented Apple LP64 serialization
overload fix inside a disposable copy. The one runtime change to libmorph removes
its no-op `__stack_chk_fail` definition, preserving the platform's stack protection.
No compiler hardening flags are weakened.

## Reproduce

Provide local Git checkouts containing the above three revisions, then run:

```sh
python3 Vendor/RussianMorphology/tools/regenerate.py \
  --libmorph /absolute/path/to/libmorph \
  --moonycode /absolute/path/to/moonycode \
  --mtc /absolute/path/to/mtc
swift test --jobs 2 --package-path Vendor/RussianMorphology \
  --scratch-path .build/russian-morphology-tests
```

The generator reads pinned Git objects instead of working-tree edits and compares
all generated bytes. It requires Python 3.12+ and clang++; it downloads nothing.
Its temporary checkout copies, compiler processes and outputs are deleted on exit.

## Contract and limits

`SensitiveDictionaryMorphologySnapshot()` is stateless and Sendable. Its
`forms(for:)` returns a complete bounded set for the dictionary interpretations
of one known word, or `nil` for an unknown word. It throws on invalid input,
native failure or an output paradigm exceeding its resource bounds; it never publishes
partial forms or invents an unverified suffix rule. Native input is capped at 128
UTF-8 bytes, native interpretations at 64, generated forms at 512, and output at
65,536 bytes. Long tokens and non-Russian scripts return `nil` for exact matching.
Callers may impose smaller admission budgets.

Ambiguous spellings include all dictionary interpretations. This intentionally
favours coverage over contextual disambiguation. Morphology does not establish
that a word is sensitive, find synonyms, or distinguish meanings such as a
technical rollback. It does not invent forms for unknown proper names, ASR
misspellings or unsupported languages. A caller should retain exact matching
and expose manual variants for those cases. Matching words in a phrase does not
require constructing the Cartesian product of their paradigms.

Native tables are immutable process image data. Each synchronous call owns its
temporary native and Swift buffers and finishes before returning. There are no
resident models, background tasks, sockets or separate unload operations.
